facts.statement: Chucarosaurus is an extinct genus of titanosaurian dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Chucarosaurus (meaning "indomitable reptile") is an extinct genus of titanosaurian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Albian) Huincul Formation of Argentina.

facts.statement: The genus Chucarosaurus contains only one known species, C. diripienda, which is known from limb and pelvic bones.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, C. diripienda, known from various limb and pelvic bones.

facts.statement: The genus and species Chucarosaurus diripienda were described by Agnolin et al. in 2023.
facts.quote: In 2023, Agnolin et al. described Chucarosaurus diripienda, a new genus and species of colossosaurian titanosaurs, based on these fossil remains.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered at the Pueblo Blanco Natural Reserve in Río Negro Province, Argentina, within the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The Chucarosaurus holotype specimen, MPCA PV 820, was discovered in sediments of the Huincul Formation, dated to the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous period, at Pueblo Blanco Natural Reserve in Río Negro Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen consists of various limb and pelvic bones belonging to a single individual.
facts.quote: The specimen consists of a complete left humerus, partial left radius, complete left metacarpal II, left ischium, partial left femur and fibula, partial right tibia, and partial indeterminate metapodial, all of which belong to one individual.

facts.statement: Chucarosaurus was a large dinosaur with slender limbs.
facts.quote: Chucarosaurus was a large, slender-limbed titanosaur.

facts.statement: The femur of Chucarosaurus was roughly 1.9 meters long.
facts.quote: Its femur was roughly 1.9 m long, somewhat smaller than the estimated 2.5 m length of the femur of Argentinosaurus.

facts.statement: Chucarosaurus is classified as a colossosaurian member of the Titanosauria, closely related to a clade containing Notocolossus and the Lognkosauria.
facts.quote: Agnolin et al. (2023) recovered Chucarosaurus as a colossosaurian member of the Titanosauria, as the sister taxon to a clade formed by Notocolossus and the Lognkosauria.

facts.statement: Chucarosaurus lived in the Early Cretaceous Huincul Formation of Río Negro Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Chucarosaurus is known from the Early Cretaceous Huincul Formation of Río Negro Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: Chucarosaurus lived between 110.1 and 106.3 million years ago during the Albian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (110.1 to 106.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Huincul Formation also yielded fossils of diverse dinosaurs including titanosaurs, abelisaurids, carcharodontosaurids, and avetheropods.
facts.quote: Many dinosaurs, including fellow titanosaurs (Argentinosaurus Bustingorrytitan, and Choconsaurus), rebbachisaurids (Cathartesaura, Cienciargentina, Limaysaurus, and Sidersaura), carcharodontosaurids (Mapusaurus, Meraxes, and Taurovenator), a megaraptoran (Aoniraptor), abelisaurids (Skorpiovenator, Tralkasaurus, and Ilokelesia), an elaphrosaurine (Huinculsaurus), a paravian (Overoraptor), and the unusual avetheropod Gualicho have also been named from the formation.

rejected.quote: The generic name, "Chucarosaurus", combines "chucaro", a Quechua word meaning "hard and indomitable animal" with the Latin word "saurus", meaning "reptile".
